title: One task list, a blocked calendar and messages on your terms

say: One task list, a blocked calendar, and messages on your terms.
This is the video for Module 2 of Productivity and Time Management at Work.
Many of us keep work in our heads, on scraps of paper, and in starred WhatsApp chats. The result is a constant feeling of something forgotten.

say: David Allen, author of Getting Things Done, says the mind is for having ideas, not holding them. So first, capture everything into one inbox, such as a pinned Google Keep note.

items: Capture everything into one inbox
Clarify: is it actionable?
Under two minutes? Do it now
Organise: next actions, waiting for, projects
Review weekly, then do the work

say: On Monday morning Grace feels overwhelmed and cannot say what is on her plate.
In 15 minutes she writes 31 items into a Keep note, from her notebook, starred WhatsApp messages and two sticky notes.
She deletes or files 4 and does 6 small ones on the spot. The rest become 13 next actions, 5 projects, and 3 follow-ups.
In about 45 minutes, she knows exactly what to do first.
A task list says what. A calendar says when. A task with a time is far more likely to happen. Put fixed meetings in first.

Name the block with the action

Leave a buffer in the afternoon

say: Then block 60 to 120 minutes for your most important task, in your best-energy hours.

say: Batching means doing similar tasks together, like all calls, or all supplier payments, in one block. Each switch costs you time getting back in.

say: The Pomodoro Technique was named after a tomato-shaped kitchen timer. Work on one task for 25 minutes without switching. If a thought interrupts you, write it in your inbox.

cards.d: Choose one task and work on it without switching.
Take a short break. Stand, stretch, drink water.
Take a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes.

say: Then take a short break of about 5 minutes.

cards.d: Choose one task and work on it without switching.
Take a short break. Stand, stretch, drink water.
Take a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes.

say: After four sessions, take a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes.
For example, Chioma, a sales manager in Abuja, runs her monthly sales review as four Pomodoros from 9 to 11, and finishes by 11 instead of late at night.

say: For many of us, WhatsApp is where work happens. The goal is not to ignore people. It is to decide when you deal with messages.
Open them in a batch, and give each one a decision. Delete it, do it if it takes under two minutes, delegate it, or defer it to a task.

panel.heading: The four Ds for every message
items: Delete or archive it
Do it, if under two minutes
Delegate it to the right person
Defer it to a task or snooze

say: Bukola's baseline showed 28 WhatsApp interruptions a day, and only 30 minutes of focused menu planning.
She moves customer chats to WhatsApp Business and creates 5 quick replies, such as her price list, delivery areas and how to pay.
She mutes 6 non-urgent groups and checks them once a day. She answers messages at 8, 12:30 and 4, and her profile tells customers to call for emergencies.
After two weeks her interruptions fall to about 6 a day, and she gets close to 2 focused hours each morning. Customers still get answers within a few hours.

Batching also gives you time to check messages calmly. Be suspicious of urgent payment requests, new account numbers from suppliers, or messages claiming to be from your bank. Call a number you already know.

panel.heading: Check messages calmly
items: Be suspicious of urgent payment requests
Confirm new account numbers by phone
Call a number you already know

say: And never share OTPs or PINs on WhatsApp. Do not keep passwords or your BVN in Keep notes either.

say: To remember. Capture into one inbox and clarify every item. Write next actions that start with a verb. Block your most important task first. Focus in 25-minute sprints. And batch your messages, giving each one of the four Ds.

panel.heading: Remember
items: One inbox, then clarify every item
Next actions start with a verb
Block your top task first
25 minutes focus, then a short break
Batch messages: delete, do, delegate, defer
